title: Disney History Mystery
theme: Company history: dates, acquisitions, firsts and famous places
intro: [excited] Grab your magnifying glasses! Tonight we're going back in time to solve the mysteries of Disney company history. [laughs] Dates, deals, firsts, and secrets!

art.prompt: A cozy history archive with tall shelves of film canisters, an old desk with a magnifying glass, a vintage map, and a glowing castle model, warm lamplight Original illustration, 16:9, rich saturated colors, cinematic lighting, no people, no characters, no text, no logos.

categories.title: Founding Years
categories.intro: [excited] Calendars out! Every answer in this one is a year from Disney history. [chuckles] No time machine needed.

art.prompt: A stack of old calendar pages blowing in the wind over a vintage film camera, an antique clock and a small model castle, sepia glow Original illustration, 16:9, rich saturated colors, cinematic lighting, no people, no characters, no text, no logos.

clues.clue: Walt and Roy Disney founded the Disney Brothers Cartoon Studio on October 16 of this year.
clues.reveal: [excited] The correct answer is 1923! Disney turned 100 in 2023. Happy birthday, old friend.

clues.clue: Disneyland opened in Anaheim on July 17 of this year.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is 1955! [laughs] Opening day was a mess. Disney called it Black Sunday.

clues.clue: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs premiered in December of this year.
clues.reveal: [excited] The correct answer is 1937! People called it Disney's Folly. Then it became a huge hit.

clues.clue: EPCOT Center opened at Walt Disney World on October 1 of this year.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is 1982! [chuckles] Exactly eleven years after Magic Kingdom opened.

clues.clue: Walt Disney Productions first sold its stock to the public in this year, to help pay for big projects.
clues.reveal: [excited] The correct answer is 1940! Disney had big debts and big dreams, so it went public.

categories.title: Big Buys
categories.intro: [laughs] Shopping spree! Name the company Disney bought. [whispers] It's a lot more expensive than a churro.

art.prompt: A giant golden shopping cart overflowing with miniature film studio buildings, a lightsaber-like glowing beam, a superhero shield, and a satellite dish Original illustration, 16:9, rich saturated colors, cinematic lighting, no people, no characters, no text, no logos.

clues.clue: In 2006, Disney bought this animation studio, the maker of Toy Story.
clues.reveal: [excited] The correct answer is Pixar! Disney had been working with them for years. Then it just bought them.

clues.clue: In 2009, Disney bought this comic book company, home of Spider-Man and Iron Man.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Marvel! [laughs] Avengers, assemble... at Disney.

clues.clue: In 2012, Disney bought this company and with it the Star Wars franchise.
clues.reveal: [excited] The correct answer is Lucasfilm! About four billion dollars. The Force is strong with that deal.

clues.clue: In 1996, Disney finished buying Capital Cities, the parent company of this TV network.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is ABC! [chuckles] Now Disney owns the news, too.

clues.clue: In 2019, Disney finished buying most of this company's film and TV business, getting The Simpsons.
clues.reveal: [gasps] The correct answer is 21st Century Fox! It cost about 71 billion dollars. That's a lot of churros.

categories.title: Disney Firsts
categories.intro: [excited] First place! Every answer here is a famous Disney first. [laughs] Let's see who comes in first, too.

art.prompt: A shining gold first-place trophy on a pedestal surrounded by an old film reel, a paintbrush, a top hat and confetti Original illustration, 16:9, rich saturated colors, cinematic lighting, no people, no characters, no text, no logos.

clues.clue: This 1937 film was Disney's first full-length animated feature.
clues.answer: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs
accept: snow white and the seven dwarfs
choices: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs
clues.reveal: [excited] The correct answer is Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs! Heigh-ho, it's off to history we go.

clues.clue: Released in 1928, this was the first Mickey cartoon with sound to be released.
clues.reveal: [laughs] The correct answer is Steamboat Willie! Mickey was whistling from the start.

clues.clue: This 1932 Silly Symphony was the first cartoon in full Technicolor and won the first Oscar for Best Cartoon Short.
clues.reveal: [excited] The correct answer is Flowers and Trees! Color cartoons changed everything.

clues.clue: Fantasia introduced this early stereo sound system, made for movie theaters.
clues.reveal: [gasps] The correct answer is Fantasound! Sound coming from all around you. In 1940!

clues.clue: In 1987, this actor from The Absent-Minded Professor was named the very first Disney Legend.
clues.reveal: [excited] The correct answer is Fred MacMurray! The first Disney Legend. Very cool trivia.

categories.title: History Hideouts
categories.intro: I'll show you a photo of a real place from Disney history. [whispers] You tell me the place or the city.

art.prompt: An old map of America with glowing pins on four cities, a vintage film camera, an old studio key and a model castle sitting on top Original illustration, 16:9, rich saturated colors, cinematic lighting, no people, no characters, no text, no logos.

clues.clue: This 1955 castle was the first one at a Disney park. Name it.
choices: Le Château de la Belle au Bois Dormant
clues.reveal: [excited] The correct answer is Sleeping Beauty Castle! It looks small, but it has a lot of history.

clues.clue: Walt Disney was born in this house on December 5, 1901. Name the city.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Chicago! [chuckles] Walt was a city kid before he moved to a farm in Marceline.

clues.clue: This covered Main Street is in the first Disney park outside the United States, opened in 1983. Name the park.
clues.reveal: [excited] The correct answer is Tokyo Disneyland! World Bazaar has a glass roof, so you don't get wet.

clues.clue: Walt's Laugh-O-Gram studio in this city went bankrupt before he left for California. Name the city.
clues.reveal: [sighs] The correct answer is Kansas City! It didn't work out, but Walt kept going.

clues.clue: This 1940 building housed Disney animators at the studio in this California city. Name the city.
clues.reveal: [excited] The correct answer is Burbank! The Animation Building was where a lot of classic films were made.

categories.title: Mouse House Mysteries
categories.intro: [whispers] The final category is a mystery. These are the secret stories behind Disney history. [chuckles] Put on your detective hats.

art.prompt: A detective's desk with a magnifying glass, a dusty old film reel, a vintage rabbit-eared plush shadow, a tiny toy train, and a lamp in a dark office Original illustration, 16:9, rich saturated colors, cinematic lighting, no people, no characters, no text, no logos.

clues.clue: Walt's first name idea for Mickey was reportedly this, until his wife Lillian said no.
clues.reveal: [laughs] The correct answer is Mortimer! Lillian saved the day. Mortimer just doesn't sound as nice.

clues.clue: Before Mickey, Walt made cartoons about this lucky rabbit, but lost the rights in 1928.
clues.reveal: [sighs] The correct answer is Oswald the Lucky Rabbit! Losing him led to Mickey, so it all worked out.

clues.clue: In 2006, Disney got Oswald back by letting this sportscaster leave for NBC.
clues.reveal: [laughs] The correct answer is Al Michaels! Traded for a cartoon rabbit.

clues.clue: This animator worked with Walt and drew the first Mickey Mouse cartoons.
clues.reveal: [excited] The correct answer is Ub Iwerks! He was super fast at drawing.

clues.clue: Walt built this small backyard railroad at his home in Holmby Hills.
clues.reveal: [excited] The correct answer is the Carolwood Pacific Railroad! Walt loved trains so much that he built one at home.
